name: Custard Pudding No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: a tablespoonful of peach-water or other flavor
ingredients.originalText: a tablespoonful of peach-water or other flavor
ingredients.quantityText: a tablespoonful of peach-water or other flavor

instructions.text: Pour one quart of milk in a deep pan and let the pan stand in a kettle of boiling water
Beat to a cream eight eggs and six tablespoonfuls of fine sugar and a teaspoon of flour
Stir the eggs and sugar into the milk and continue stirring until it begins to thicken
Remove the pan from the boiling water, scrape down the sides, stir to the bottom until it begins to cool
Add a tablespoonful of peach-water, or any other flavor you may prefer
Pour into little cups and, when cold, serve

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Pour one quart of milk in a deep pan and let the pan stand in a kettle of boiling water
2. Beat to a cream eight eggs and six tablespoonfuls of fine sugar and a teaspoon of flour
3. Stir the eggs and sugar into the milk and continue stirring until it begins to thicken
4. Remove the pan from the boiling water, scrape down the sides, stir to the bottom until it begins to cool
5. Add a tablespoonful of peach-water, or any other flavor you may prefer
6. Pour into little cups and, when cold, serve
